stops.note: 'terror, fear', brought by Viking settlers; it replaced the native Old English ege
'awe' + '-ful': worthy of reverent fear, as God or a king was
the weakened sense 'very bad' is recorded by 1809; in 1794 Hester Lynch Piozzi had already scolded well-bred ladies for using 'awful' too lightly

current_meaning: very bad or unpleasant; (old) inspiring awe
